transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. Let's lock the Q3 roadmap today. Top of the list is the v2 onboarding flow, which is basically done - nice work. What's next after that ships?

transcript.speaker: Priya Nandakumar
transcript.text: Two big candidates: the API redesign Jae-won's been pushing for, and expanding SSO support for enterprise customers. We can't do both in parallel with the current team size.

transcript.speaker: Jae-won Lee
transcript.text: The API redesign removes a lot of tech debt but it's not customer-visible. SSO is directly blocking three enterprise deals sales is working right now.

transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: How many deals exactly, and how big?

transcript.speaker: Sofia Marchetti
transcript.text: I heard from sales it's three deals, combined around 400k in annual contract value, all blocked on SAML SSO specifically, not just OAuth.

transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: That settles it for me - SSO first. Let's prioritize SAML SSO support for Q3, and push the API redesign to Q4.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nandakumar
transcript.text: Agreed, that's the right call given the revenue on the table.

transcript.speaker: Jae-won Lee
transcript.text: I can start scoping SAML integration this week. I'd estimate five to six weeks for a solid implementation, including admin configuration UI.

transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: Sofia, can design get started on the SSO admin settings screen in parallel?

transcript.speaker: Sofia Marchetti
transcript.text: Yes, I'll have wireframes ready within a week so Jae-won isn't blocked.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nandakumar
transcript.text: We should also budget time for at least one enterprise customer to pilot SSO before general availability - I don't want our first SAML integration tested only in-house.

transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: Good point. Let's pencil in a two-week pilot with one of the three deals once it's feature-complete, before we call it done.

transcript.speaker: Jae-won Lee
transcript.text: Makes sense. One open question - do we need to support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO flows, or just one? That changes scope meaningfully.

transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: I don't know off the top of my head. Let's find out from the three prospects which flow their IT teams actually require before we scope further.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nandakumar
transcript.text: I'll reach out to sales this week to get that from the prospects.

transcript.speaker: Derek Osei
transcript.text: Perfect. To summarize: SAML SSO is the Q3 priority, API redesign moves to Q4, and we'll pilot with a real customer before GA.
